title: Review annotations to GO:0006090 pyruvate metabolic process

author: deustp01
body: Reactome instances have been fixed as requested, but with the observation that dividing pyruvate metabolism into synthetic and catabolic parts loses important biological information just as we would if we could not annotate NAD-dependent oxidation-reduction processes, but had to put oxidative and reductive ones into unconnected separate buckets.

author: ValWood
body:
Hi @deustp01 apologies, that wasn't the intention. I assumed you would be able to annotate everything to a specific descendant pathway  rather than biosynthetic or catabolic terms. I was able to for fission yeast. Are there any pathways missing that should be there?

Note that the correct fermentative pathways should be there after this ticket is addressed:
https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/29511

author: ValWood
body:
Actually I see that gluconeogenesis does not always go through pyruvate, but usually does so this would be an issue.

I agree  that it isn't useful to move these down to catabolic/biosynthetic.

We should remove the direct annotation constraint here; sorry about that.

author: sjm41
ValWood
body: Yes, specific pathways are better, but not all pathways involving pyruvate are children of pyruvate metabolism, so I guess it can be closed.

author: deustp01
body: > I assumed you would be able to annotate everything to a specific descendant pathway rather than biosynthetic or catabolic terms. No! As posted to some other fermentation ticket pyruvate plays a critical role as a junction among metabolic pathways in mammals as shown in this cartoon I used to inflict on medical students. Making a flat list of all the metabolic processes that are involved one way or another in those junctions loses the key fact of the interactions among those pieces, as shown in the cartoon.

author: deustp01
body:
Continuing in this direction, here is a summary from a review by Carl Cori, who knew about this stuff, emphasizing the importance of the interconnections among specific processes to explain the biology (Cori 1981 - [PMID: 7273846](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7273846/)). My cartoon is an attempt to show these interconnections.

> The operation of the cycle in the regulation of the blood glucose level depends on the ability of the liver to convert 3 carbon compounds derived from glucose—mainly lactate-pyruvate, glycerol, and transaminated pyruvate—back to glucose or glycogen.

author: raymond91125
body:
> Reactome instances have been fixed as requested, but with the observation that dividing pyruvate metabolism into synthetic and catabolic parts loses important biological information just as we would if we could not annotate NAD-dependent oxidation-reduction processes, but had to put oxidative and reductive ones into unconnected separate buckets.

Sorry for being dense. I'm not sure I understand the problem. Isn't this solved by multiple parentage or multiple annotations? A NAD-dependent oxidation-reduction process would have parentage to both oxidation and reduction branches of metabolism. When a gene is annotated to a broad term, we wouldn't know if it's not well understood or it's involved in more than one child process. In contrast, if it's annotated to multiple child processes, the annotations are automatically propagated up to the broad.

>Making a flat list of all the metabolic processes that are involved one way or another in those junctions loses the key fact of the interactions among those pieces, as shown in the cartoon.

But annotating to the broad term of pyruvate metabolism does not help to illuminate the intricacies either; only a GO-CAM model can provide the expressivity, I think.

author: deustp01
body:
> But annotating to the broad term of pyruvate metabolism does not help to illuminate the intricacies either; only a GO-CAM model can provide the expressivity, I think.

Agreed. But maybe that is a general point about classic GO annotations and GO-CAMs - the former are atomic assertions while the latter are intended to capture connections among the atoms (and do it really well), so there's no need to try to stuff extra connectivity into single GO terms.

body: Any more objections to adding do_not_annotate? Thanks.
